defaults.prefix: Do not use any tools. Do not read any files. Answer with the final answer only.

questions.prompt: Write the integers from 1 to 100 in order. How many times does the digit 7 appear in what you wrote?
questions.hint: 7 appears 10 times in the tens place (70-79) and 10 times in the units place (7, 17, ... 97), and 77 is counted once in each, so 20.

questions.prompt: Three consecutive integers add up to 87. What is the largest of the three?
You have 27 identical-looking balls. Exactly one is lighter than the others. Using a balance scale, what is the fewest number of weighings that guarantees finding the lighter ball?
questions.hint: Each weighing has three outcomes, so three weighings separate 3^3 = 27 possibilities.

questions.prompt: A basket holds 5 red balls and 7 blue balls. You take balls out without looking. What is the smallest number you must take to be certain of having at least one ball of each colour?
questions.hint: The worst case is drawing all 7 blue balls first, so 8 guarantees a red.

questions.prompt: Start with the string "abcde". Reverse it. Append the letter f to the end. Then delete the second character of the result. What is the final string?
questions.hint: abcde -> edcba -> edcbaf -> ecbaf (the second character, d, is removed).

questions.prompt: Reply with exactly one line in this form, substituting your own values: status=OK retries=0. Use zero retries.
questions.hint: Demonstrates a regex grader. The capture group is the extracted value; a separate `answer` would be compared against it.

questions.prompt: Reply with exactly three words, each different from the others and none of them a number.
questions.script:
words = text.split()
result = (len(words) == 3
          and len(set(w.lower() for w in words)) == 3
          and not any(w.isdigit() for w in words))
questions.hint: Demonstrates a script grader. The script is evaluated with `text` bound to the reply and must leave a boolean in `result` (or be a bare expression).
